subject: Human Evolution
title: Social Meals
description: A quick win: understand Social Meals.

hook.text: Chimps eat alone, grabbing food and turning away. Humans gather around a shared meal. Why the shift?

buildup.text: Cooking creates a delay between getting food and eating it. That window invites competition—or sharing.

discovery.text: Sharing cooked food built reciprocity: I cook for you today, you share your hunt with me tomorrow.

twist.text: The campfire meal may have been the original social contract—a nightly ritual of trust and exchange.

climax.text: Eating together reinforced pair bonds, alliances, and group identity in ways eating alone never could.

punchline.text: Dinner tables built the first communities.

quiz.question: How did cooking change social behavior?
options: Shared meals built reciprocity and group bonds
